newsitem.title: UK: NatWest slips as analyst briefings continue.
newsitem.headline: NatWest slips as analyst briefings continue.

text.p: Shares in National Westminster Bank Plc eased on Wednesday as briefings between bank executives and sector analysts prompted downgrades in profit estimates, analysts said.
NatWest shares slipped 5-1/2p to 798-1/2p by 1140 GMT.
The latest to cut earnings estimates was Salomon Brothers analyst John Leonard who trimmed by 70 million stg for this year to 1,825 million stg and to 2,055 million from 2,125 million for 1998.

In 1996 the company made pre-tax profits of 1,122 million stg. Leonard said the reductions followed a reassessment of NatWest's comments at its recent annual meeting, with margins seen under pressure in its UK banking business and expenses growing, especially due to technology investments.

On Tuesday, SocGen also lowered its NatWest earnings estimates, bringing its top-end figures in line with the market consensus, yet the outlook for the bank's shares is probably more tied up with recent talk of possible bids and mergers in the bank sector, dealers said.

NatWest has been seen as under pressure to do a deal, possibly with a domestic rival such as Abbey National Plc, to improve shareholder returns and tackle the recent underperformance of its shares, they said.
Last week ABN AMRO Hoare Govett cut its estimates by 130 million stg to 1,820 million stg for 1997 and by 100 million to 2.3 billion for next year after a meeting with the bank.
Hoare analysts said they based the downgrade on higher than expected bad debts and losses(of about 77 million)incurred by NatWest Markets through options trading.
SBC Warburg and UBS are due to see NatWest next week.
A NatWest spokesman said, "What we are talking about is all public information but we would not comment on specific discussions."
NatWest reports half-year results on August 5.
